result.title: An actively trained neural operator for near-explicit atmospheric chemistry
result.summary: Earth-system models simplify atmospheric chemistry into condensed mechanisms, because near-explicit mechanisms such as the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM) are too costly to solve in every grid cell. Neural emulators could lift this limit, but most advance the chemistry in small time steps and cover only a few species or a reduced mechanism. Here we introduce FNO-MoE, a Fourier neural operator with a mixture of experts that predicts the full near-explicit chemical state over 30 minutes in a single call. The same network also guides its own training, using the disagreement among its experts to select the most informative box-model simulations. At equal cost, this active sampling yields a more accurate emulator than random or evenly spread sampling. Fine-tuning on longer trajectories keeps it stable over multi-hour runs in which models trained on short simulations diverge. The resulting emulator reproduces the evolution of thousands of species with high fidelity, remains accurate for unseen chemical compositions and runs orders of magnitude faster than the numerical solver. These results open a new direction for emulating complex atmospheric systems: neural operators that predict the full chemical state over long windows and choose their own training data. Training under changing meteorology is the next step towards bringing near-explicit chemistry into Earth-system models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FNO-MoE，将傅里叶神经算子与专家混合结合，单次调用预测 30 分钟后的完整近显式大气化学状态，并利用专家间分歧主动挑选训练样本、再经长轨迹微调维持多小时稳定。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「以专家分歧主动选择训练轨迹」和「单次长窗口预测全状态」可能为 LVR 的训练样本/监督分配与并行状态更新提供可核查线索。
